content.title: About
content.content: Grilled bass fillet is a tender, lean white fish with a subtle nutty flavor. Bass is farmed in clean lakes and rivers, and grilling preserves most of its nutrients while adding a smoky aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bass belongs to the Percidae family and is one of the most popular grill fish in Europe and North America.
Its omega‑3 fatty acid content is higher than many marine fish because of a diet rich in algae.
Traditionally, whole bass is grilled over open fire, but fillets are more convenient for quick cooking.
In Japan, bass fillets are often marinated in soy sauce and lemon juice before grilling to enhance flavor.
Bass can grow up to 2.5 kg, but most commercial fillets come from fish weighing 0.5–1 kg.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, lower triglyceride levels, and have anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Bass fillet provides all essential amino acids, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many sea fish, bass has a modest fat content, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12, B6 and niacin help maintain nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and phosphorus
items.content: Selenium protects cells from oxidative stress, while phosphorus is essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy metal contamination
items.content: Although bass generally contains low mercury levels, it is advisable to source fish from clean waters.

items.title: Possible parasites
items.content: Insufficient cooking can leave parasites alive; ensure the internal temperature reaches at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve grilled bass fillet hot, drizzled with lemon juice or a sauce made from olive oil and fresh herbs. It pairs well with roasted vegetables, quinoa, mashed potatoes, or a crisp salad. For extra tenderness, marinate the fillet beforehand in a mixture of lemon, garlic, and rosemary.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh bass fillets in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C, wrapped in plastic film or in an airtight container, for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C in a sealed bag, where they retain quality for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking; discard if the fish smells sour or feels slimy.
